newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Walloon Region in 100 bln Bfr CP programme.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Walloon Region in 100 bln Bfr CP programme.

text.p: Belgium's Walloon Region will launch a 100 billion Belgian franc treasury bill programme, the region's budget minister Jean-Claude Van Cauwenberghe told a news conference on Thursday.

"This programme covers all maturities between one and 10 years and allows the region therefore to issue commercial paper, with a maximum one year maturity, as well as medium term notes," lead manager and dealer Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) said.
Van Cauwenberghe said the programme was enough to cover the region's financial needs between now and the introduction of the euro as Europe's single currency in 1999.

"This amount allows us to cover, for the most part, the repayment of around 60 billion francs falling due between 1997 and 1998, but also new financing needs...of 11 billion francs for 1997, 8.6 billion for 1998 and six billion for 1999," he said.
Van Cauwenberghe said the issue would allow the region to restructure some outstanding debts and generate exceptional income of 446 million francs.
It would be the largest Belgian franc treasury bill programme by a non-federal government body, Van Cauwenberghe noted.
CCB board member Guy Schifflers said issuance would start in the first half of November after publication of a full prospectus.
He said the region wanted to raise around 30 billion francs by the end of 1996.
The duration of the programme was open, he noted.
